title: Release-train calendar optimization for rolling quantization and model-variant rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a coordinated release-train calendar and signal runway that lets Runtime, Console, and API teams roll out model quantization profiles and model-variant swaps in rolling waves with predictable capacity, observable quality metrics, and clear rollback lanes.

Context: We expect several medium-risk runtime changes in Q1: new int8 quantization profiles for Llama-family variants, a model-binary swap for a regional tier, and console UX that surfaces model variant toggles. These changes affect serving throughput, tail latency, and could cause transient quality regressions unless staged carefully. Current launch windows are ad-hoc across teams which increases blast radius.

Scope: This ticket defines the launch calendar cadence, gating signals, capacity reservation policy, and communications choreography for rolling quantization and model-variant rollouts spanning Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployment channels. It does NOT include the low-level kernel rollout plan (ENG runtime to own) but will capture when and how that plan is exercised across customers and regions.
acceptance_criteria: A shared release-train calendar exists for the next 12 weeks with clear owner for each wave and region
Gating checklist documented and signed by Runtime, Console, API, and SRE leads (latency SLOs, error budget threshold, quality regression signal)
Capacity reservations and burst lanes defined per regional pool and dedicated tenant tiers
Communication and rollback runbooks published with templates for customer-notify, status pages, and on-call escalation
Two rehearsals executed (one dry-run with shadow traffic and one canary with 5% traffic) and results captured in postmortem-style notes

runbook_summary: Wave pattern: phase-0 shadow (2d) -> phase-1 regional canary (3 regions, 5% traffic, 72h) -> phase-2 staggered ramp (24h steps to 100% per region). Gating signals: latency P95, error_rate, golden-sets quality score, and resource utilization. Rollback policy: automated rollback if any signal breaches for 2 consecutive 15m windows or manual rollback by SRE lead. Communication: pre-launch RFC -> T-48h notify customers on affected tenants -> T-0 status page + Slack channel + post-launch notes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected tail-latency increase from new kernels. Mitigation: Shadow traffic and kernel-level feature flags to toggle optimized kernels per host.
Risk: Quality regressions on edge prompts. Mitigation: Run golden-set evals every hour during canary and hold ramp if regression > 2%.
Risk: Dedicated tenant capacity constraints. Mitigation: Pre-reserve burst lanes and coordinate with Sales/Account teams for temporary quota increases.
Risk: Console toggle causes confusion. Mitigation: UX copy reviewed; show 'beta' badge + telemetry opt-in + link to opt-out docs.
